intended_object: An auxiliary helper for the Hasse–Weil constant-extension argument. It contracts a height-one prime q of S ⊗_C O_N to an ideal of O_N, where O_N is the integral closure of C[X] in N under the reciprocal-polynomial (place-at-infinity) algebra structure. The contraction is along the map b ↦ 1 ⊗ b. This reading comes from the docstring and from how the proof files use it.
explanation: The body is just `Ideal.comap` along `Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight`, applied to `q.asIdeal`. That correctly computes the contraction ("downstairs ideal") the docstring describes, so nothing is wrong. But it is a named shorthand for one concrete instance of Mathlib's general `Ideal.comap`, set up inside a heavily specialised context: local instances for the reciprocal-polynomial algebra, the tensor product with a constant field extension S/C, and so on. It is a proof device for the infinity-place bridge lemmas, used only in three files of this development. It is not an independent mathematical notion that should be judged for generality. Ideal contraction itself already exists in full generality in Mathlib as `Ideal.comap`.
